  <entry>
    <id>tag:appaddict.app,2005:Post/18356</id>
    <published>2026-06-16T16:13:07Z</published>
    <updated>2026-06-16T16:13:09Z</updated>
    <link rel="alternate" type="text/html" href="https://appaddict.app/post/supasidebar-boosts-privacy-and-productivity"/>
    <title>SupaSidebar Boosts Privacy and Productivity</title>
    <content type="html">&lt;figure class="attachment attachment--preview flex-col justify-center attachment--jpeg"&gt;
    &lt;img class="lightbox__image strip-metadata lightbox__image" alt="SupaSidebar in Action" src="https://scribbles.page/rails/active_storage/representations/proxy/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBBL2l1QVE9PSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--e3233b5db8fdcef758567db6c14bcbe5c1ca6e54/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaDdDRG9MWm05eWJXRjBTU0lKYW5CbFp3WTZCa1ZVT2hSeVpYTnBlbVZmZEc5ZmJHbHRhWFJiQjJrQ0FBaHBBZ0FHT2dwellYWmxjbnNIT2dwemRISnBjRlE2REhGMVlXeHBkSGxwWkE9PSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoidmFyaWF0aW9uIn19--fa3dbe24e376882dfd8c9dddfec0441143a8bd41/39977.jpeg" loading="lazy" decoding="async"&gt;
    &lt;figcaption class="attachment__caption text-center"&gt;
      SupaSidebar in Action
    &lt;/figcaption&gt;
&lt;/figure&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Most technically oriented people who value privacy do so because privacy is, and should be, a human right, not because they have something to hide.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Maintaining privacy in the current technical environment requires a real strategy and almost constant attention to an evolving landscape.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It is no longer enough to block trackers, ads, and cookies. Browser fingerprinting has become one of the primary privacy-violating mechanisms used by companies that want to identify, profile, and monetize you across the web.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;One strategy many people use is spreading their work across multiple browsers. That has a second benefit: it lets you match the strengths of a particular browser to the task at hand.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Privacy and Productivity&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The downside becomes obvious pretty quickly: you take a real productivity hit when your history, bookmarks, and open tabs are scattered across multiple places.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There are several tools that try to help with this. The one I like best is &lt;a href="https://supasidebar.com"&gt;SupaSidebar&lt;/a&gt;, by developer Kshetez Vinayak. He stands out for being responsive, helpful, and clearly invested in fixing bugs and expanding the app’s usefulness. I bought SupaSidebar during the 2025 Black Friday sale and have been using it ever since.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;SupaSidebar operates at the OS level. It is not a browser extension. It is built for exactly this use case: people who use multiple browsers and need a way to consolidate browser context without paying a constant productivity tax every time they switch.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Arc was a favorite of many Mac power users, and for good reason. Although it is still maintained for security, active feature development effectively stopped in early 2025. Arc introduced a genuinely useful way to manage browsing around spaces, context, and workflows. SupaSidebar recreates much of that experience, but does it across multiple browsers instead of inside just one.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The power of SupaSidebar becomes obvious when you take the time to create spaces that match how you actually work. You might have a space for research, one for personal browsing, one for work, and separate spaces for projects that need to stay isolated.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Within a space, SupaSidebar aggregates tabs and bookmarks from every supported browser you have open. It pulls in Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Arc, and others. You get a vertical, organized, searchable interface showing your open tabs across browsers.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If your browser use is simple, the free version may be enough. It supports three spaces. Paid users get unlimited spaces.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;SupaSidebar also has a command panel with fuzzy search across tabs, bookmarks, history, folders, and spaces. It works like a specialized version of Spotlight for your internet life.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Features&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Some of the most useful features include:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;
&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Recents tab&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;: shows recently visited tabs across browsers, which is useful for recovering something without keeping every tab open and burning RAM&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;
&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Multiple ways to save links&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;: right-click, drag-and-drop, command panel, auto-routing rules, and more&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;
&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Notes for saved links&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;: add context to a link without leaving the app&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;
&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Browser profile linking&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;: connect a space to a specific browser profile so links open in the right place automatically&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;
&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Auto-routing rules&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;: send links to specific spaces or browser profiles based on conditions&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;
&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;AI chat mode&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;: integrates with OpenAI, Anthropic, and Gemini directly in the panel, with Markdown rendering and slash commands&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Yes, But...&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;SupaSidebar is still, at its core, a beta app. But it has a clear purpose, it is actively developed, and it solves a real problem that many multi-browser power users have simply learned to tolerate.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The spaces model gives it more depth than simple tab aggregation. The pricing is also reasonable, and the free tier is actually useful.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Free&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;: 0-3 spaces&lt;br&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Pro&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;: $13.99/year with unlimited spaces, early access, and priority support&lt;br&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Lifetime&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;: $34.99 one-time purchase, 5 devices, lifetime updates&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Use &lt;code&gt;BETA30&lt;/code&gt; as a discount code for 30% off both paid options.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There are bugs and rough edges. I have seen tab synchronization inconsistencies, occasional lag when opening folders, and occasional page reloads when clicking tabs. The command panel also has some edge-case quirks around keyboard navigation.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;But even with those issues, SupaSidebar is one of the more useful workflow apps I have added to my Mac setup recently.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If you stick with one browser for everything, you probably will not get much out of it. But if you live across Safari, Firefox, Chrome, Arc, and browser profiles, SupaSidebar fills a gap that Apple, Google, and Mozilla have not bothered to solve.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href="mailto:lou@louplummer.lol?subject=SupaSidebar%20Boosts%20Privacy%20and%20Productivity" style="text-decoration: underline"&gt;✉️ Reply by email&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;</content>

  <entry>
    <id>tag:appaddict.app,2005:Post/18172</id>
    <published>2026-06-01T21:02:01Z</published>
    <updated>2026-06-13T06:48:45Z</updated>
    <link rel="alternate" type="text/html" href="https://appaddict.app/post/cache-out-a-privacy-focused-free-tool-for-multiple-browsers"/>
    <title>Cache Out - A Privacy Focused Free Tool For Multiple Browsers</title>
    <content type="html">&lt;figure class="attachment attachment--preview flex-col justify-center attachment--jpg"&gt;
    &lt;img class="lightbox__image strip-metadata lightbox__image" src="https://scribbles.page/rails/active_storage/representations/proxy/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBBK2FyQVE9PSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--109a148300c16e76fceb7baf00fb800ed209c139/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaDdDRG9MWm05eWJXRjBTU0lJYW5CbkJqb0dSVlE2RkhKbGMybDZaVjkwYjE5c2FXMXBkRnNIYVFJQUNHa0NBQVk2Q25OaGRtVnlld2M2Q25OMGNtbHdWRG9NY1hWaGJHbDBlV2xrIiwiZXhwIjpudWxsLCJwdXIiOiJ2YXJpYXRpb24ifX0=--daf4078a1aefa3c961be2c7b8fbe4a74a2641c0c/CleanShot%202026-06-01%20at%2017.00.35@2x.jpg" loading="lazy" decoding="async"&gt;
&lt;/figure&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href="https://cacheout.app/"&gt;Cache Out&lt;/a&gt;, a free new single-purpose utility from veteran Mac developer Jim Mitchell, fits right into an app category that is severely underrepresented - utilities that work across multiple browsers from a single interface.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;What It Does&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Cache Out's superpower is selective data removal from a variety of popular macOS browsers with the click of a single button. It removes five categories of information - &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;cache, history, downloads, favicons, and cookies&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;. You select the browsers you want cleared from a list. You select the categories of data to remove. Then, you click a single button and BOOM. It's done. After the files are removed, you aren't left in the dark about what happened since you get a report on the number of files and MBs that were removed.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There are currently seven supported browsers:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Safari&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Chrome&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Firefox&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Edge&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Brave&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Opera&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Orion&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;I'd like to see a few more on the list, including Vivaldi, Arc, and Atlas. Thankfully, Mitchell indicates that more browsers are coming.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Cache Out punches all the right buttons for a privacy-focused app. It doesn't phone home or collect analytics. It doesn't require an account or registration. It's Apple-notarized. Everything happens on your machine.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Why You Need It&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Don't think that an app like this is the ultimate Boss Button. Most corporate-owned computers track Internet traffic in real time, so your IT department can still track your history if this is your only precaution. Still, most undermanned and overworked support workers don't care where you go as a general rule. Likewise, your home ISP can track your DNS requests for almost every site you visit unless you use a no-log VPN or a service like NextDNS that offers name resolution over HTTPS. Even then, you have to be savvy enough to set it up correctly.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Still, there are a lot of reasons for running clean browsers. In a world where browser fingerprinting is maximally invasive and pervasive, one defense is using multiple browsers to make yourself harder to track for the data scrapers of the world. You'll quickly build up GBs of data for almost every browser you use. If you're stuck with a small hard drive you can't upgrade (like my brand-new M4 Mac Mini's 256GB), you always have to be careful with space. Cache Out is the perfect app to do that.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Also, many countries, including my own, are seeing a rollback of civil liberties. To make matters worse, areas where people travel with their computers offer less privacy than you'd have at home. If you gave the slightest concern about the TSA, ICE, or the CBP looking through your browser history, use Cache Out before you travel.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;2026-06-13 Update&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Cache Out has been updated to v1.3.1, adding several new features:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;New &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Preview before cleaning&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt; option: see exactly which files and download-history rows would be removed, and confirm, before anything is deleted.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;New &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Move to Trash instead of deleting&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt; option, so cleared files are recoverable.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Each browser card now shows its &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;reclaimable size&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt; in the header, calculated at launch.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;New &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Clean default profile only&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt; preference for multi-profile browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Opera, Brave).&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Clearing browsing history now also clears the &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;“Recently Closed”&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt; tabs and windows that browsers restore from session data.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Added &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;French localization&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Hardened the deletion safety checks against symlink and path-traversal escapes.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Other Cross Browser Utilities&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Here are utilities that operate across multiple browsers on macOS:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;hr&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;History &amp;amp; Data Aggregation&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;
&lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/historyhound-a-must-have-research-tool-1"&gt;HistoryHound a Must Have Research Tool | AppAddict&lt;/a&gt;&lt;br&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;St. Clair Software&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt; — Indexes and searches browsing history from multiple browsers (Safari, Chrome, Firefox, and more) in one place. Lets you do full-text searches across all your browser histories simultaneously. Useful for finding pages you visited without remembering which browser you used.&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;hr&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Macro &amp;amp; Automation Tools&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;
&lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/keyboard-maestro-the-app-that-makes-everything-better-tips-for-the-for-the-automation-curious"&gt;Keyboard Maestro, The App That Makes Everything Better - Tips for the Automation Curious | AppAddict&lt;/a&gt;&lt;br&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Stairways Software&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt; — A powerful macro utility that can trigger actions in any browser. You can build macros that work in Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Arc, and others — filling forms, clicking elements, navigating pages, or switching between browsers automatically.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;
&lt;a href="https://www.alfredapp.com/"&gt;Alfred&lt;/a&gt;&lt;br&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Running with Crayons&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt; — Launcher and automation tool with workflows that can interact with multiple browsers. Can open URLs in a chosen browser, search history, and trigger browser-based actions via custom workflows.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;
&lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/how-to-get-the-most-from-raycast"&gt;How to Get The Most from Raycast | AppAddict&lt;/a&gt;&lt;br&gt;A launcher and productivity tool with extensions for Chrome, Safari, Firefox, and Arc. Extensions let you search tabs, bookmarks, and history across browsers from a single interface.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;hr&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Password Managers (Cross-Browser)&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;
&lt;a href="https://1password.com/"&gt;1Password&lt;/a&gt;&lt;br&gt;Works via browser extensions in Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Edge, and Brave. The Mac app itself manages credentials centrally regardless of which browser you use.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;
&lt;a href="https://bitwarden.com/"&gt;Bitwarden&lt;/a&gt;&lt;br&gt;Open-source password manager with extensions for virtually every major browser. The Mac desktop app serves as a central vault across all of them.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;hr&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Ad Blocking &amp;amp; Privacy (System-Wide)&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;
&lt;a href="https://adguard.com/en/adguard-mac/overview.html"&gt;AdGuard for Mac&lt;/a&gt;&lt;br&gt;Filters ads and trackers at the system level, meaning it works across &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;all&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt; browsers without needing individual extensions installed in each one.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;
&lt;a href="https://www.obdev.at/products/littlesnitch/"&gt;Little Snitch&lt;/a&gt;&lt;br&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Objective Development&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt; — Network monitor and firewall that works at the OS level, so it monitors and controls outgoing connections from any browser equally.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;hr&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Developer / Inspection Tools&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;
&lt;a href="https://proxyman.io/"&gt;Proxyman&lt;/a&gt;&lt;br&gt;A macOS proxy tool that intercepts HTTP/HTTPS traffic from any browser (or app). Useful for debugging web traffic regardless of which browser made the request.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;
&lt;a href="https://www.charlesproxy.com/"&gt;Charles Proxy&lt;/a&gt;&lt;br&gt;Similar to Proxyman — a web debugging proxy that captures traffic from all browsers at the network level.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;hr&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Bookmark Management&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;
&lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/raindrop-io-gets-a-significant-new-feature"&gt;Raindrop.io Gets a Significant New Feature | AppAddict&lt;/a&gt;&lt;br&gt;Cross-browser bookmark manager with extensions for all major browsers. Centralizes bookmarks saved from any browser into one organized collection.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;
&lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/goodlinks"&gt;GoodLinks | AppAddict&lt;/a&gt;&lt;br&gt;Read-later and bookmarking app with Safari extension built-in and support for sharing from other browsers via the share sheet.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

  <entry>
    <id>tag:appaddict.app,2005:Post/18146</id>
    <published>2026-05-27T18:21:17Z</published>
    <updated>2026-05-27T18:21:20Z</updated>
    <link rel="alternate" type="text/html" href="https://appaddict.app/post/just-wondering-around-github-looking-for-a-software-fix"/>
    <title>Just Wondering Around Github, Looking for a Software Fix</title>
    <content type="html">&lt;figure class="attachment attachment--preview flex-col justify-center attachment--png"&gt;
    &lt;img class="lightbox__image strip-metadata lightbox__image" src="https://scribbles.page/rails/active_storage/representations/proxy/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBBMytyQVE9PSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--8e948e39099201cafe5bac929eb53a7d19e06c3e/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaDdDRG9MWm05eWJXRjBTU0lJY0c1bkJqb0dSVlE2RkhKbGMybDZaVjkwYjE5c2FXMXBkRnNIYVFJQUNHa0NBQVk2Q25OaGRtVnlld2M2Q25OMGNtbHdWRG9NY1hWaGJHbDBlV2xrIiwiZXhwIjpudWxsLCJwdXIiOiJ2YXJpYXRpb24ifX0=--768aeab7fb7843d85fe5b2b4ba237e06e6ef604f/github-gold-blog-header-fixed.png" loading="lazy" decoding="async"&gt;
&lt;/figure&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The mark of a good Internet citizen is whether they star the GitHub repositories they like and whether they upvote helpful posts on Reddit. As someone who devotes a lot of time to online communities, racking up a few Internet points always feels good. I used to be slightly intimidated by GitHub. For the most part, it's full of indie apps by individual devs, so there isn't a marketing department designing websites and writing copy. It's just the same dude who coded the app you want to try. If you spend time looking around, you find that GitHub also contains plenty of goodies that aren't apps. There are repositories for scripts, app settings, Black Friday deals, and more. I'm not a dev, but even I have a couple of public repos. On one, I share my collection of &lt;a href="https://github.com/cyclelou/Automation"&gt;800 Keyboard Maestro macros, plus Hazel rules and Better Touch Tool actions&lt;/a&gt;. My other public repo is &lt;a href="https://github.com/cyclelou/Amerpie"&gt;a collection of markdown documents&lt;/a&gt; with quotes from people wiser than me. I added over 300 new notes there last week.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;One obsessive soul created a repo where he &lt;a href="https://github.com/marekbrze/categorized-obsidian-plugins"&gt;documented 1,600 Obsidian extensions&lt;/a&gt; AND another for &lt;a href="https://github.com/marekbrze/categorized-raycast-extensions"&gt;1,700 Raycast extensions&lt;/a&gt;. It's impossible, I think, to keep something like that up to date, but both are good resources.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/page/appaddict-s-github-bookmarks"&gt;You can see a list of 81 repositories I felt worthy of being added to my Raindrop collection here&lt;/a&gt;. Here are a few highlights. I'm always looking for more, so hit me up if you have anything to share.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;macOS Apps &amp;amp; Utilities&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;&lt;a href="https://github.com/mas-cli/mas"&gt;MAS&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Command-line interface for the &lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Mac App Store&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;. Search, install, update, and manage App Store apps from the terminal. Easy to use as part of a launchd item or cron job to force updates when the Mac App Store is being stubborn about doing it for you.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;&lt;a href="https://github.com/tw93/Mole"&gt;Mole&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Terminal-based tool for cleaning, uninstalling, analyzing, optimizing, and monitoring your Mac. This is the free version that does almost everything the GUI (which is not free) does.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;&lt;a href="https://github.com/cardisoft/Cardinal"&gt;Cardinal&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Fast macOS file search app using Everything-compatible syntax with filters for file type, size, tags, and content.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Obsidian&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;&lt;a href="https://github.com/LilSizzles/Obsidian-Webclipper-Templates"&gt;Obsidian Webclipper Templates&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Customizable Obsidian Webclipper templates with LLM integration that automatically organize and categorize clipped web content into structured notes. I've tried every way known to mankind to get selected web content into my vault.&lt;/p&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;This is the way.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;&lt;a href="https://github.com/sylumer/automators"&gt;Automators Vault&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Obsidian vault for the late great Automators Podcast community, containing automation-related notes, show notes, and resources.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Raycast&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;&lt;a href="https://github.com/raycast/script-commands"&gt;script-commands&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Official Raycast collection of community-contributed script commands you can install and run directly from the launcher.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;&lt;a href="https://github.com/WToa/raycast_extensions_by_downloads"&gt;raycast_extensions_by_downloads&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Auto-generated, regularly updated ranking of Raycast extensions sorted by download count.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Automation and Scripting&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Tools for automating tasks on macOS and the command line.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;&lt;a href="https://github.com/charmbracelet/gum"&gt;Gum&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Charm tool for writing interactive shell scripts with styled prompts, spinners, and formatted output.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;&lt;a href="https://github.com/topgrade-rs/topgrade"&gt;Topgrade&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Single command to upgrade everything on your system -- The Mac App Store, package managers, Homebrew apps, runtimes, and more -- all at once. See also &lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/topgrade-upgrade-all-the-things"&gt;Topgrade - Upgrade All the Things | AppAddict&lt;/a&gt; and &lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/how-to-use-topgrade-silently-and-automatically-for-multiple-update-protocols-free"&gt;How to Use Topgrade Silently and Automatically for Multiple Update Protocols (Free) | AppAddict&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Privacy, Networking and Security&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;&lt;a href="https://github.com/glinford/dns-easy-switcher"&gt;DNS Easy Switcher&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Simple macOS app for quickly switching between DNS server configurations.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;&lt;a href="https://github.com/yokoffing/Betterfox"&gt;Betterfox&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Firefox &lt;code&gt;user.js&lt;/code&gt; configuration file for optimal privacy and security hardening without breaking normal browsing.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Curated Lists &amp;amp; Directories&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Awesome lists, resource hubs, and community-maintained directories.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;&lt;a href="https://github.com/jaywcjlove/awesome-mac"&gt;awesome-mac&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;High-quality, community-curated list of macOS software, tools, and resources organized by category.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;&lt;a href="https://github.com/serhii-londar/open-source-mac-os-apps"&gt;open-source-mac-os-apps&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Comprehensive list of open-source macOS applications available for free, organized by type.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;&lt;a href="https://github.com/mRs-/Black-Friday-Deals"&gt;Black-Friday-Deals&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Community-maintained list of Black Friday deals on macOS/iOS software and books, updated annually.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;AI &amp;amp; Language Models&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Tools for running, hosting, and working with AI and local language models.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;&lt;a href="https://github.com/Arthur-Ficial/apfel"&gt;apfel&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Exposes Apple's built-in on-device language model as a local OpenAI-compatible API server on macOS. Enables AI capabilities without cloud APIs or API keys.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;&lt;a href="https://github.com/Mozilla-Ocho/llamafile"&gt;llamafile&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Distribute and run LLMs as a single self-contained executable file. Removes the complexity of setting up local models across platforms.&lt;/p&gt;

As someone who devotes a lot of time to online communities, racking up a few Internet points always feels good. I used to be slightly intimidated...</summary>

    <id>tag:appaddict.app,2005:Post/18142</id>
    <published>2026-05-27T00:33:51Z</published>
    <updated>2026-05-27T00:33:52Z</updated>
    <link rel="alternate" type="text/html" href="https://appaddict.app/post/why-i-replaced-jettison-with-ejectify-after-15-years"/>
    <title>Why I Replaced Jettison with Ejectify after 15 Years</title>
    <content type="html">&lt;figure class="attachment attachment--preview flex-col justify-center attachment--jpeg"&gt;
    &lt;img class="lightbox__image strip-metadata lightbox__image" src="https://scribbles.page/rails/active_storage/representations/proxy/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBBMm1yQVE9PSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--e18ed26c89be1f83d3207e138c79627f8b454faf/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaDdDRG9MWm05eWJXRjBTU0lKYW5CbFp3WTZCa1ZVT2hSeVpYTnBlbVZmZEc5ZmJHbHRhWFJiQjJrQ0FBaHBBZ0FHT2dwellYWmxjbnNIT2dwemRISnBjRlE2REhGMVlXeHBkSGxwWkE9PSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoidmFyaWF0aW9uIn19--fa3dbe24e376882dfd8c9dddfec0441143a8bd41/81673.jpeg" loading="lazy" decoding="async"&gt;
&lt;/figure&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In trying to be open-minded, I recently agreed to try &lt;a href="https://ejectify.app/"&gt;Ejectify&lt;/a&gt;, an app that performs a task for which I already had a solution: to automatically eject external disks from my Mac before it goes to sleep and to remount them when it wakes. I worked off a MacBook for a long, long time, and I needed a way to just shut it, unplug, and move on without getting nagged to death about thumb drives and external volumes. I've been using &lt;a href="https://stclairsoft.com/Jettison/"&gt;Jettison&lt;/a&gt; to do that since I saw it in Macworld in 2011. The developer, St. Clair Software, also makes &lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/default-folder-x-an-og-app-for-mac-power-users"&gt;Default Folder X&lt;/a&gt;, &lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/historyhound-a-must-have-research-tool-1"&gt;History Hound&lt;/a&gt;, and &lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/app-tamer-from-st-claire-software"&gt;App Tamer&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The reason I opted to try Ejectify is that it ticks some boxes that are pretty important in 2026. It's &lt;a href="https://github.com/nielsmouthaan/ejectify-macos"&gt;open source and on Github&lt;/a&gt;, meaning you can essentially get it for free if you have the chops to build it. You can also see how the developer, Niels Mouthaan, responds to issues, both in troubleshooting and in planning for additional features. I've used &lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/backup-status-check-up-your-time-machine"&gt;other apps from Niels&lt;/a&gt;, and he has provided me with good support.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Aside from philosophical differences with Jettison, there are also some features added by using Ejectify.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Volumes are managed individually, not as one size fits all, so you have more control.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Provides a way to force unmount a disk on a case-by-case basis.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Allows you to mute "Disks Not Ejected Properly" messages if you and macOS can't reach an agreement on what that means.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;The full feature set (from the website):&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Helps prevent "Disk Not Ejected Properly" notifications after wake.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Helps reduce the risk of data loss or corrupted volumes by safely unmounting them first.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Lets you choose which supported volumes Ejectify manages, including external volumes, ejectable internal volumes, and disk images.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Supports automatic unmounting when the display turns off or the system starts sleeping, then attempts to mount volumes again after wake.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Includes force unmount, force mute notifications, and instant "Unmount all" actions, plus a global keyboard shortcut for manual unmount-all.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href="mailto:lou@louplummer.lol?subject=Why%20I%20Replaced%20Jettison%20with%20Ejectify%20after%2015%20Years" style="text-decoration: underline"&gt;✉️ Reply by email&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;</content>
    <summary>

In trying to be open-minded, I recently agreed to try Ejectify, an app that performs a task for which I already had a solution: to automatically eject external disks from my Mac before it goes to sleep and to remount them when it wakes. I worked off a MacBook for...</summary>

    <id>tag:appaddict.app,2005:Post/18120</id>
    <published>2026-05-24T01:46:46Z</published>
    <updated>2026-05-24T01:46:48Z</updated>
    <link rel="alternate" type="text/html" href="https://appaddict.app/post/10-ways-to-get-more-out-of-apple-shortcuts"/>
    <title>10 Ways to Get More Out of Apple Shortcuts</title>
    <content type="html">&lt;figure class="attachment attachment--preview flex-col justify-center attachment--jpg"&gt;
    &lt;img class="lightbox__image strip-metadata lightbox__image" src="https://scribbles.page/rails/active_storage/representations/proxy/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBBd3FyQVE9PSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--07bb5d91e3d113c723a743e7b7c566c89f24944a/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaDdDRG9MWm05eWJXRjBTU0lJYW5CbkJqb0dSVlE2RkhKbGMybDZaVjkwYjE5c2FXMXBkRnNIYVFJQUNHa0NBQVk2Q25OaGRtVnlld2M2Q25OMGNtbHdWRG9NY1hWaGJHbDBlV2xrIiwiZXhwIjpudWxsLCJwdXIiOiJ2YXJpYXRpb24ifX0=--daf4078a1aefa3c961be2c7b8fbe4a74a2641c0c/playground.jpg" loading="lazy" decoding="async"&gt;
&lt;/figure&gt;

&lt;p&gt;I like using Apple Shortcuts when it fits my workflow, but advanced features can be confusing. I manage simple loops and variables, but it’s slow and tricky. That’s why I was happy to see MacStories release Shortcuts Playground, a free plugin for Codex and Claude Code. It lets you describe what you want in natural language and creates a real Apple Shortcut you can use or share. You can &lt;a href="https://www.macstories.net/shortcuts-playground/"&gt;read about it and get installation instructions&lt;/a&gt; for free if you have those platforms.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It’s been years since I updated my list of free and cheap apps that boost Apple Shortcuts, so here’s the 2026 edition.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Best Standalone App for Triggers - Shortery&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Apps like Keyboard Maestro, Hazel, and BetterTouchTool can trigger Shortcuts but take time to learn. &lt;a href="https://apps.apple.com/us/app/shortery/id1594183810?mt=12"&gt;Shortery&lt;/a&gt; costs $29.99 and is easier to use. Apple also added some automation triggers in macOS:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;macOS Shortcuts covers basics&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li class="lexxy-nested-listitem"&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Apps, Files and folders, Wi‑Fi/Bluetooth, Displays, Focus, Time, Wake/sleep&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Shortery adds extras&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li class="lexxy-nested-listitem"&gt;&lt;ul&gt;&lt;li&gt;Audio, Camera, Clamshell, Calendar, Keyboard hotkeys, Login/logout, LAN, Power details, Screen lock/unlock, Sunrise/sunset, More device triggers&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Best Deep System Control: Shortcutie&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For $10, &lt;a href="https://sindresorhus.gumroad.com/l/shortcutie"&gt;Shortcutie&lt;/a&gt; offers 70+ system actions Apple won’t allow directly. It can change defaults without prompts, clear all notifications, quit all apps, scrape browser tabs, run JavaScript, and grab selected text from any window.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Best for Extra Shortcut Actions: Toolbox and Actions.app&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Sindre Sorhus’s free app Actions offers 170 Shortcut actions for all Apple platforms. See a partial list &lt;a href="https://sindresorhus.com/actions"&gt;here&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href="https://apps.apple.com/us/app/toolbox-pro-for-shortcuts/id1476205977"&gt;Toolbox Pro&lt;/a&gt; costs $5.99 one-time and adds powerful features for date/time, dictionaries, contacts, files, media, reminders, system tasks, and text.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Best for Persistent Data: Data Jar&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Shortcuts handle temporary data well but can’t save it long-term. &lt;a href="https://apps.apple.com/us/app/data-jar/id1453273600"&gt;Data Jar&lt;/a&gt; (donationware) stores structured data for Shortcuts to read and update later, helping workflows track state over time—making Shortcuts act like apps.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Good for: settings, preferences, counters, lists, saved variables, workflow state.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Best for Notes-Centric Workflows: Actions for Obsidian&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href="https://apps.apple.com/us/app/actions-for-obsidian/id1659667937"&gt;Actions for Obsidian&lt;/a&gt; adds Shortcut features to import web content, calendars, contacts, health data, and more into Obsidian notes.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Other Useful Shortcut Enhancers&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;
&lt;a href="https://actions.work/barcuts/"&gt;BarCuts: macOS Shortcuts Launcher&lt;/a&gt; — menu bar app shows relevant Shortcuts without clutter &lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;
&lt;a href="https://menubox.app/"&gt;Menu Box&lt;/a&gt; — create custom Shortcut menus&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Find helpful Shortcuts at:&lt;br&gt;&lt;a href="https://routinehub.co/"&gt;Routine Hub&lt;/a&gt;&lt;br&gt;&lt;a href="https://matthewcassinelli.com/"&gt;Matthew Cassinelli&lt;/a&gt;&lt;br&gt;&lt;a href="https://shortcutsgallery.com/"&gt;Shortcuts Gallery&lt;/a&gt;&lt;br&gt;&lt;a href="https://www.macstories.net/shortcuts/"&gt;MacStories Shortcuts Archive&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href="mailto:lou@louplummer.lol?subject=10%20Ways%20to%20Get%20More%20Out%20of%20Apple%20Shortcuts" style="text-decoration: underline"&gt;✉️ Reply by email&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;</content>
    <summary>I like using Apple Shortcuts when it fits my workflow, but advanced features can be confusing. I manage simple loops and variables, but it’s slow and tricky. That’s why I was happy to see MacStories release Shortcuts Playground, a free plugin for Codex and Claude Code. It lets you describe...</summary>

  <entry>
    <id>tag:appaddict.app,2005:Post/18110</id>
    <published>2026-05-21T15:11:07Z</published>
    <updated>2026-05-21T15:11:09Z</updated>
    <link rel="alternate" type="text/html" href="https://appaddict.app/post/marked-3-is-the-markdown-companion-a-lot-of-mac-writers-have-been-waiting-for"/>
    <title>Marked 3 Is the Markdown Companion a Lot of Mac Writers Have Been Waiting For</title>
    <content type="html">&lt;figure class="attachment attachment--preview flex-col justify-center attachment--jpeg"&gt;
    &lt;img class="lightbox__image strip-metadata lightbox__image" src="https://scribbles.page/rails/active_storage/representations/proxy/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBBK2FxQVE9PSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--eebfa283ec02775fd6d2e57cd8380bd254377f1f/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaDdDRG9MWm05eWJXRjBTU0lKYW5CbFp3WTZCa1ZVT2hSeVpYTnBlbVZmZEc5ZmJHbHRhWFJiQjJrQ0FBaHBBZ0FHT2dwellYWmxjbnNIT2dwemRISnBjRlE2REhGMVlXeHBkSGxwWkE9PSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoidmFyaWF0aW9uIn19--fa3dbe24e376882dfd8c9dddfec0441143a8bd41/65281.jpeg" loading="lazy" decoding="async"&gt;
&lt;/figure&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Brett Terpstra has released &lt;a href="https://markedapp.com/"&gt;Marked 3&lt;/a&gt;, and this is not just a routine update. It’s one of those releases that makes you stop and think about where a tool actually fits in your workflow. If you write in Markdown on a Mac, there’s a very good chance Marked has been the missing piece all along.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For years, I lived in Microsoft Word for anything that wasn’t email. That was the EdTech world: Word was the standard, `.doc` and `.docx` were the expected formats, and no one wanted to hear about alternatives. Never mind the huge app footprint, the licensing mess, the cost, or the absurdity of the entire Office suite when all you really needed was a word processor.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;And whenever someone in tech tried to suggest something leaner — OpenOffice, Google Docs, anything that didn’t come with Microsoft baggage — the pushback was immediate and emotional. In 2015, we were literally one day away from canceling our Microsoft contract when the superintendent made a late-afternoon phone call to my boss with a $100K purchase order to renew. That was the kind of environment it was.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;So yes, I value the freedom to choose my own tools now.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Plain text has become the backbone of the way I work. Obsidian handles notes and longer writing. Drafts is where quick capture happens. Blogging tools and publishing platforms fill in the rest. Markdown wasn’t hard to learn, and once it clicks, it’s hard to go back. But Markdown has one weakness: the writing experience is only as good as the tools around it.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That’s where Marked comes in.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Marked Defined&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Marked is not an editor. That’s the first thing to understand. It works alongside your editor, taking Markdown and rendering it live so you can actually see what your writing looks like without breaking your flow.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It also works with HTML and OPML files, which makes it more flexible than a lot of people realize. And beyond rendering, Marked can convert documents to PDF, HTML, DOCX, and RTF. It also brings prose analysis, syntax checking, and integration with all sorts of writing and outlining apps.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Who It’s For&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The short answer: anybody who writes.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If you’re a coder or a technical writer, you get a lot of useful extras:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Syntax highlighting for code blocks&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;MathJax and KaTeX support&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Mermaid diagrams&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;MultiMarkdown, YAML, and Pandoc metadata support&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;CriticMarkup&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That’s useful, sure, but it’s not really why I care about it.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For the kind of writing I do, the most valuable features are the ones that help me clean up my prose before I hit publish:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Spelling and grammar checking&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Sentence simplification tips&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Word count, sentence count, and sentence complexity&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Reading time&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Grade-level scoring&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That’s the real value. Write where you’re comfortable, then let Marked tell you what the page actually looks like.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;The Little Things That Make It Better&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Marked has a bunch of features that sound minor until you actually start using them regularly. Flexible search. Automatic table of contents generation. Bookmarking. A visual document overview. Collapsible sections. Keyboard access almost everywhere.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;It’s also a very nice Markdown reader, even when you’re not editing. Auto-scroll is there. So is distraction-free mode. And if you want to read faster, there’s even an RSVP-style overlay with adjustable WPM.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If you work with outlines or mind maps, Marked supports embeds from popular apps and can even turn an outline into a mind map directly. That’s a niche feature, but a genuinely useful one if your brain works that way.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There are also browser extensions for sending page URLs or selected content straight into Marked 3, which is a nice touch if you spend any time collecting notes from the web.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Integrations Matter&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Marked works the way good Mac software should: it gets out of the way and plays well with the tools you already use.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That means it fits alongside Scrivener, Word, MarsEdit, Bear, Ulysses, Obsidian, and other writing apps. In v3, Scrivener rendering with live preview is new, and Bear and Obsidian callouts are now fully supported.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;And for the automation crowd, there’s CLI support and AppleScript. That alone makes it much more interesting than a typical “pretty preview” app.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Final Thoughts&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If you have a Setapp subscription, Marked 3 is already there. Otherwise, you can &lt;a href="https://markedapp.com/download/Marked.zip"&gt;download it directly&lt;/a&gt; for a free trial or pick it up from the &lt;a href="https://apps.apple.com/us/app/marked-3/id6747497179?mt=12"&gt;Mac App Store.&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The lifetime price is $69.99, which is a little steep, though not outrageous for a serious utility you’ll keep using. The subscription option is $2.99 per month, which is much easier to justify.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Marked 3 is the kind of Mac app that quietly improves everything around it. It doesn’t try to replace your editor. It makes your writing workflow better by giving you a clearer view of what you’ve actually written, and that’s a pretty compelling trick.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;And in classic Brett Terpstra fashion, it’s built by someone who clearly understands the people using it.&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href="mailto:lou@louplummer.lol?subject=Marked%203%20Is%20the%20Markdown%20Companion%20a%20Lot%20of%20Mac%20Writers%20Have%20Been%20Waiting%20For" style="text-decoration: underline"&gt;✉️ Reply by email&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;</content>

  <entry>
    <id>tag:appaddict.app,2005:Post/18063</id>
    <published>2026-05-14T19:41:36Z</published>
    <updated>2026-05-15T08:22:08Z</updated>
    <link rel="alternate" type="text/html" href="https://appaddict.app/post/airspace-a-polished-fix-for-a-macos-friction-point"/>
    <title>Airspace: A Polished Fix for a macOS  Friction Point</title>
    <content type="html">&lt;figure class="attachment attachment--preview flex-col justify-center attachment--jpg"&gt;
    &lt;img class="lightbox__image strip-metadata lightbox__image" src="https://scribbles.page/rails/active_storage/representations/proxy/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBBeldxQVE9PSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--4a398873ec647aec88651331e1caf38a100f61e5/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaDdDRG9MWm05eWJXRjBTU0lJYW5CbkJqb0dSVlE2RkhKbGMybDZaVjkwYjE5c2FXMXBkRnNIYVFJQUNHa0NBQVk2Q25OaGRtVnlld2M2Q25OMGNtbHdWRG9NY1hWaGJHbDBlV2xrIiwiZXhwIjpudWxsLCJwdXIiOiJ2YXJpYXRpb24ifX0=--daf4078a1aefa3c961be2c7b8fbe4a74a2641c0c/lists.Ciy44Y24.jpg" loading="lazy" decoding="async"&gt;
&lt;/figure&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href="https://hazels.garden/airspace"&gt;Airspace&lt;/a&gt;, an app I downloaded today, has a lot going for it. It removes a classic Apple friction point by letting you name your virtual desktops, customize their appearance, and assign keyboard shortcuts to jump between them. It also helps me illustrate a point.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Making a decision about the right price for an app has to be one of the hardest parts of releasing something new.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Some of the most versatile and useful apps in the Mac ecosystem are priced absurdly low. I am looking at you, &lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/better-touch-tool-favorite"&gt;BetterTouchTool&lt;/a&gt;. On the other hand, we have all seen apps with plenty of competitors that still carry what I consider an absurdly high price. My favorite example is the clipboard manager, &lt;a href="https://pasteapp.io/pricing"&gt;Paste&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In reality, every software purchase comes down to what we value. Some people have strict requirements around aesthetics and would rather pay for polish than use something more functional. I think the ebook manager Calibre fits that description perfectly. I love it and use it every day for its incredible versatility, but it certainly is not easy on the eyes.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Two of my favorite notch apps show how wide the pricing spread can be. &lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/new-droppy-release-is-a-full-featured-utility-suite"&gt;Droppy&lt;/a&gt;, which is not just a notch app but a full suite of utilities, costs 10 euro. Dynamic Lake, another app I like in this space, costs 40% more, still a fair price. It is well thought out and nicely designed, but it is much more narrowly focused on the notch.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;There are personal factors, too. I live in the United States. I am retired. I have disposable income that I dedicate to buying software. I compensate by driving a 2005 Toyota and not playing golf like some of my contemporaries. But there are plenty of tech enthusiasts in less prosperous countries, students on tight budgets, and people for whom software pricing is a much more serious decision point than it is for me.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Now, more about Airspace.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Features&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Custom Naming&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;br&gt;Instead of Desktop 1, Desktop 2, and so on, you can have Writing, Development, Social, or whatever names fit the way you actually work.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Visual Personalization&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;br&gt;You can choose custom colors for the menu bar indicator and switcher menu, making different Spaces easier to recognize at a glance.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;User-Defined Shortcuts&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;br&gt;You can assign your own shortcuts to switch between Spaces. If your writing tools live on Desktop 3, make &lt;code&gt;Cmd+Option+3&lt;/code&gt; the shortcut that takes you there.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Multi-Monitor Support&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;br&gt;If you use a Mac mini or a laptop with an external display, you will appreciate that Airspace works across displays. It also handles selected full-screen apps, with one important exception noted below.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;HUD Overlay&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;br&gt;The current release supports a heads-up display switcher that shows your custom Space names and colors.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Selling Points&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;No AI used in development, backed by documentation such as GitHub history, Figma files, and browser logs. Whether that matters to you depends on your stance on AI-assisted development, but it is refreshing to see the work documented transparently.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Full-featured seven-day trial.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Fully sandboxed and App Store approved, while still delivering the core functionality many users want.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;No tracking or data collection.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Caveats&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Airspace v1. did not track Spaces created by clicking the green traffic-light full-screen button. AirSpace v2.1 (latest) added this feature, so if you are on the previous version, make sure to upgrade.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Onboarding is a process, not an event. If you use as many Spaces as I do, it takes a few minutes to get Airspace configured.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;There is no Mission Control integration. Custom names will not appear in Mission Control. That is an Apple limitation; Airspace cannot modify that UI. The workaround is to use Airspace's own menu bar indicator and HUD instead.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Similar Apps and Solutions&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;You can achieve some of what Airspace does with a &lt;a href="https://www.hammerspoon.org/"&gt;Hammerspoon&lt;/a&gt; script or a &lt;a href="https://www.keyboardmaestro.com/main/"&gt;Keyboard Maestro&lt;/a&gt; macro. There are also direct competitors like &lt;a href="https://www.jaysce.dev/projects/spaceman"&gt;Spaceman&lt;/a&gt; and &lt;a href="https://contexts.co"&gt;Contexts&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href="https://www.josean.com/posts/how-to-setup-aerospace-tiling-window-manager"&gt;Aerospace&lt;/a&gt;, a tiling window manager beloved by people who like to fiddle, offers virtual workspace emulation that is similar in spirit, but it is not a true Spaces replacement.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Details&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Developer's website: &lt;a href="https://hazels.garden/airspace"&gt;https://hazels.garden/airspace&lt;/a&gt;
&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Privacy policy: &lt;a href="https://hazels.garden/privacy"&gt;https://hazels.garden/privacy&lt;/a&gt;
&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Price: $9.99&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;Bottom Line&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Airspace is not trying to reinvent window management on the Mac. It's not a window manager at all.It is trying to make Apple's existing Spaces feature more usable, more readable, and faster to navigate. That is a narrow job, but it is a real one.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;At $9.99, the price feels fair to me, especially if you already rely on Spaces as part of your daily workflow. If you only use one or two desktops, this probably will not change your life. But if you live across several named work contexts, Airspace turns a vague row of numbered desktops into something much closer to an actual workspace system.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;figure class="attachment attachment--preview flex-col justify-center attachment--jpeg"&gt;
    &lt;img class="lightbox__image strip-metadata lightbox__image" src="https://scribbles.page/rails/active_storage/representations/proxy/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBBemVxQVE9PSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--4d9d39c1f7906fb9ae04bfdb37764552a5c34169/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaDdDRG9MWm05eWJXRjBTU0lKYW5CbFp3WTZCa1ZVT2hSeVpYTnBlbVZmZEc5ZmJHbHRhWFJiQjJrQ0FBaHBBZ0FHT2dwellYWmxjbnNIT2dwemRISnBjRlE2REhGMVlXeHBkSGxwWkE9PSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoidmFyaWF0aW9uIn19--fa3dbe24e376882dfd8c9dddfec0441143a8bd41/94468.jpeg" loading="lazy" decoding="async"&gt;
&lt;/figure&gt;

    <summary>Airspace, an app I downloaded today, has a lot going for it. It removes a classic Apple friction point by letting you name your virtual desktops, customize their appearance, and assign keyboard shortcuts to jump between them. It also helps me illustrate a point.

  <entry>
    <id>tag:appaddict.app,2005:Post/18054</id>
    <published>2026-05-13T16:45:57Z</published>
    <updated>2026-05-13T16:45:59Z</updated>
    <link rel="alternate" type="text/html" href="https://appaddict.app/post/dockdoor-pro-the-dock-apple-wouldn-t-build"/>
    <title>DockDoor Pro - The Dock Apple Wouldn't Build</title>
    <content type="html">&lt;figure class="attachment attachment--preview flex-col justify-center attachment--jpg"&gt;
    &lt;img class="lightbox__image strip-metadata lightbox__image" src="https://scribbles.page/rails/active_storage/representations/proxy/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBBL0NwQVE9PSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--d4417eca27835b0dec300375d1d28c12a71e5b8f/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaDdDRG9MWm05eWJXRjBTU0lJYW5CbkJqb0dSVlE2RkhKbGMybDZaVjkwYjE5c2FXMXBkRnNIYVFJQUNHa0NBQVk2Q25OaGRtVnlld2M2Q25OMGNtbHdWRG9NY1hWaGJHbDBlV2xrIiwiZXhwIjpudWxsLCJwdXIiOiJ2YXJpYXRpb24ifX0=--daf4078a1aefa3c961be2c7b8fbe4a74a2641c0c/CleanShot%202026-05-13%20at%2012.45.27.jpg" loading="lazy" decoding="async"&gt;
&lt;/figure&gt;

&lt;p&gt;When the free app DockDoor was released in 2024, it was the first time I had seen a developer add window previews to the Mac Dock in much the same way that other operating system from Redmond handles them. For kicks, it also included a Windows-style application switcher, also free.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;I have been &lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/dockdoor-adds-functionality-to-macos"&gt;updating some older reviews&lt;/a&gt;, so I went back to check on DockDoor. Not only does the original free version still exist, but the developer has also added a paid Pro version with a much larger feature set.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The splash page for DockDoor Pro puts its claim front and center:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;DockDoor Pro - The Dock macOS Deserves&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;The official native Mac dock replacement with profiles, live window previews, media controls, a file tray, magnification, and everything Apple left out.&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;hr&gt;

&lt;p&gt;That is bold, but defensible.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;What It Does&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The real question with any Dock utility is whether it replaces the native Dock or merely augments it. DockDoor Pro can do either. I hid the native Dock completely and did not run into any problems.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The other killer feature, and one Apple will probably never give us for fear of waking the ghost of Steve Jobs, is the ability to exclude a running app from the Dock. You no longer have to stare at every app just because it happens to be open.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Dock Profiles&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt; - I work in multiple contexts. Some of my time is spent testing software and writing reviews. For that, I need quick access to a file manager, an uninstaller, Activity Monitor, Drafts, Obsidian, my Downloads folder, the folder where I keep rough drafts, the folder where I keep archives, and Reddit.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;DockDoor Pro profiles can include:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Pinned apps&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Folders&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Files&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Widgets&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;URLs&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Design elements, including separators and spacers&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;When I switch to media management, I need a different setup: &lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/calibre-keeps-getting-better"&gt;Calibre&lt;/a&gt;, &lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/swinsian-music-app-the-answer-to-feature-bloat"&gt;Swinsian&lt;/a&gt;, &lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/i-replaced-apple-music-with-yate-swinsian-navidrome-and-an-ipod-classic-surprisingly-better"&gt;Yate&lt;/a&gt;, &lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/digikam-is-replacing-apple-photos-google-photos-and-amazon-photos-for-me"&gt;digiKam&lt;/a&gt;, &amp;amp; &lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/toyviewer-a-preview-replacment"&gt;ToyViewer&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;When it is time to do research or just relax, I want &lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/inoreader-rss-gets-new-features"&gt;Inoreader&lt;/a&gt;, &lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/freetube-maybe-the-most-underrated-app"&gt;FreeTube&lt;/a&gt;, &lt;a href="https://watch.plex.tv/me"&gt;Plex&lt;/a&gt;, &lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/2025-01-07"&gt;Radarr&lt;/a&gt;, Sonarr, and websites like &lt;a href="https://macmenubar.com"&gt;Mac Menu Bar &lt;/a&gt;and &lt;a href="https://alternativeto.net/"&gt;AlternativeTo&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;DockDoor Pro gives you two ways to switch profiles. The easiest is to associate a specific app with a profile. When you open an app tied to another workflow, the Dock profile changes automatically. If you work with multiple monitors, you can also assign different Docks on a per-display basis.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;One welcome feature is the ability to export Dock profiles as JSON. That makes it easy to move a setup to another Mac or keep a restorable backup in case an experiment goes sideways.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Control Panel&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt; - Each Dock contains a tiny icon that opens a control panel when long-clicked. It consolidates an app launcher, profile switcher, volume slider, audio device picker, and power controls. It is a well-designed bit of UI rather than a pile of bolted-on buttons.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;File Tray&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt; - If you keep your Dock at the bottom of the display, scrolling on it reveals a file tray. You can drop files there temporarily, drag them back out when you need them, or send them via AirDrop directly from the tray.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Widgets&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt; - DockDoor Pro also includes small widgets that add live tiles directly to the Dock, including weather and system stats. They stay compact at rest and expand with more detail on hover. They also adapt to the Dock's design, so they do not look like afterthoughts.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The music widget is almost an app within the app. You get album art, a seek bar, and synchronized lyrics with a karaoke-style anticipation offset. Whether that is useful or just fun depends on how you work. I do not need lyrics in my Dock, but I understand the appeal.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Customization&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is the least opinionated Dock app I have used. If you are not inclined to fiddle, it looks fine out of the box. If you like to experiment, you can control almost every visible part of the UI, including:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Color&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Spacing&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Padding&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Background&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Shape&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;h3&gt;Conclusion&lt;/h3&gt;

&lt;p&gt;DockDoor Pro is still in beta, and there is a warning not to use it on a mission-critical machine, so do not install it on your boss's MacBook and blame me if something gets weird. That said, I have not encountered any instability after two weeks of constant use.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;This is an app best suited for power users, especially those with multi-monitor setups or workflows that shift throughout the day. If you use the same five apps all the time and do not care about customizing your workspace, you can probably skip it. But if you have ever wanted the Dock to be more useful, more contextual, and less stubbornly Apple-like, DockDoor Pro is worth a look.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;DockDoor Pro Website&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt; - &lt;a href="https://pro.dockdoor.net"&gt;DockDoor Pro - Official macOS Dock Replacement&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Privacy Policy&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt; - &lt;a href="https://pro.dockdoor.net/legal/"&gt;DockDoor Pro | Privacy Policy &amp;amp; EULA&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Price&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt; - $20&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href="mailto:lou@louplummer.lol?subject=DockDoor%20Pro%20-%20The%20Dock%20Apple%20Wouldn" t build style="text-decoration: underline"&gt;✉️ Reply by email&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;</content>
    <summary>When the free app DockDoor was released in 2024, it was the first time I had seen a developer add window previews to the Mac Dock in much the same way that other operating system from Redmond handles them. For kicks, it also included a Windows-style application switcher, also free....</summary>

  <entry>
    <id>tag:appaddict.app,2005:Post/18011</id>
    <published>2026-05-12T15:02:00Z</published>
    <updated>2026-05-12T09:40:36Z</updated>
    <link rel="alternate" type="text/html" href="https://appaddict.app/post/bartender-enters-a-new-era-with-top-shelf"/>
    <title>Bartender Enters a New Era with Top Shelf</title>
    <content type="html">&lt;figure class="attachment attachment--preview flex-col justify-center attachment--png"&gt;
    &lt;img class="lightbox__image strip-metadata lightbox__image" alt="Top Shelf" src="https://scribbles.page/rails/active_storage/representations/proxy/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBBemFwQVE9PSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--f453f28188bc4eb470b9e014775cee35d97db328/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaDdDRG9MWm05eWJXRjBTU0lJY0c1bkJqb0dSVlE2RkhKbGMybDZaVjkwYjE5c2FXMXBkRnNIYVFJQUNHa0NBQVk2Q25OaGRtVnlld2M2Q25OMGNtbHdWRG9NY1hWaGJHbDBlV2xrIiwiZXhwIjpudWxsLCJwdXIiOiJ2YXJpYXRpb24ifX0=--768aeab7fb7843d85fe5b2b4ba237e06e6ef604f/Top%20Shelf%20-%20Files%20(Full).png" loading="lazy" decoding="async"&gt;
    &lt;figcaption class="attachment__caption text-center"&gt;
      Top Shelf
    &lt;/figcaption&gt;
&lt;/figure&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For the past few weeks, I’ve been beta testing a new release of Bartender; an app with an interesting, and at times slightly controversial, history. Despite that, it’s a utility &lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/bartender-still-best-in-class"&gt;I’ve relied on for years&lt;/a&gt;. I recently did &lt;a href="https://appaddict.app/post/mac-menu-bar-chaos"&gt;a deep dive into the problems&lt;/a&gt; macOS changes have created for menu bar managers and what those changes mean going forward. Even with a few lingering issues in the category, I still came away viewing Bartender as the best overall option for serious Mac users.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The new release, called &lt;a href="https://www.macbartender.com/pro"&gt;Bartender Pro&lt;/a&gt;, expands beyond traditional menu bar management with a feature called Top Shelf. The idea is simple: turn the MacBook notch into something genuinely useful instead of leaving it as dead space. The developers are entering an increasingly crowded area occupied by apps like &lt;a href="https://getdroppy.app/"&gt;Droppy&lt;/a&gt; and &lt;a href="https://www.dynamiclake.com/"&gt;DynamicLake Pro&lt;/a&gt;, both of which are also trying to claim that piece of Mac interface real estate.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Top Shelf supports temporary file storage, clipboard history, AirDrop access, widgets, media controls, live weather, calendar views, and what Bartender calls “live activities.” One particularly interesting addition is support for displaying the status of running Claude Code or Codex sessions directly from the notch area. That puts Bartender Pro in direct competition with Droppy for AI-focused workflow integration.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;I’m fortunate to have a small home lab with several Macs available for testing. I’ve been running Bartender Pro on my M2 MacBook Air with the latest version of macOS, and overall the implementation feels thoughtful and mature. The developers have integrated the new functionality cleanly into Bartender’s existing settings architecture rather than bolting on a second interface.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Top Shelf interface itself is polished and visually cohesive with macOS. More importantly, it offers enough customization that power users should be able to shape it around their workflow instead of adapting to someone else’s idea of how the notch should work. Enabling or disabling features is straightforward, and the configuration process never feels overly complicated.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;One feature Bartender Pro offers that I have not seen handled as well elsewhere is its dynamic interaction with the Bartender Bar itself. The app intelligently avoids hiding menu bar items behind the notch interface, which sounds minor until you actually start using multiple notch utilities and discover how messy that problem can become.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Importantly, none of this replaces the traditional Bartender experience. The new functionality is strictly additive. Bartender 6 is still available as a standard one-time purchase for $20, and the company has been explicit that core menu bar management is not being moved behind a subscription wall.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;For users interested in Top Shelf and the broader Pro feature set, Bartender Pro is available as a $15/year subscription. That includes Bartender 6 along with all upgrades released during the subscription period.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The Bartender team has clearly invested serious effort into getting this release right. During the beta period, updates arrived constantly, feedback was actively incorporated, and bug reports received prompt attention. That responsiveness matters, especially for utility software operating this deeply inside the macOS interface.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;If you are evaluating notch utilities or trying to build a cleaner AI-oriented Mac workflow, Bartender Pro deserves a serious look.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;figure class="attachment attachment--preview flex-col justify-center attachment--png"&gt;
    &lt;img class="lightbox__image strip-metadata lightbox__image" alt="Top Shelf - General Settings" src="https://scribbles.page/rails/active_storage/representations/proxy/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBBemVwQVE9PSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--11dfe55470c659b517d16b6eb15eaef08918e296/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaDdDRG9MWm05eWJXRjBTU0lJY0c1bkJqb0dSVlE2RkhKbGMybDZaVjkwYjE5c2FXMXBkRnNIYVFJQUNHa0NBQVk2Q25OaGRtVnlld2M2Q25OMGNtbHdWRG9NY1hWaGJHbDBlV2xrIiwiZXhwIjpudWxsLCJwdXIiOiJ2YXJpYXRpb24ifX0=--768aeab7fb7843d85fe5b2b4ba237e06e6ef604f/Top%20Shelf%20Settings%20-%20General.png" loading="lazy" decoding="async"&gt;
    &lt;figcaption class="attachment__caption text-center"&gt;
      Top Shelf - General Settings
    &lt;/figcaption&gt;

    <summary>For the past few weeks, I’ve been beta testing a new release of Bartender; an app with an interesting, and at times slightly controversial, history. Despite that, it’s a utility I’ve relied on for years. I recently did a deep dive into the problems macOS changes have created for menu bar managers and...</summary>

  <entry>
    <id>tag:appaddict.app,2005:Post/17980</id>
    <published>2026-05-11T12:09:20Z</published>
    <updated>2026-05-11T12:09:21Z</updated>
    <link rel="alternate" type="text/html" href="https://appaddict.app/post/new-droppy-release-is-a-full-featured-utility-suite"/>
    <title>New Droppy Release is a Full Featured Utility Suite</title>
    <content type="html">&lt;figure class="attachment attachment--preview flex-col justify-center attachment--jpg"&gt;
    &lt;img class="lightbox__image strip-metadata lightbox__image" alt="Droppy" src="https://scribbles.page/rails/active_storage/representations/proxy/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaHBBeEdtQVE9PSIsImV4cCI6bnVsbCwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--9cb0125983217deac0e063c72c14f6392c595800/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsibWVzc2FnZSI6IkJBaDdDRG9MWm05eWJXRjBTU0lJYW5CbkJqb0dSVlE2RkhKbGMybDZaVjkwYjE5c2FXMXBkRnNIYVFJQUNHa0NBQVk2Q25OaGRtVnlld2M2Q25OMGNtbHdWRG9NY1hWaGJHbDBlV2xrIiwiZXhwIjpudWxsLCJwdXIiOiJ2YXJpYXRpb24ifX0=--daf4078a1aefa3c961be2c7b8fbe4a74a2641c0c/CleanShot%202026-05-11%20at%2007.33.52.jpg" loading="lazy" decoding="async"&gt;
    &lt;figcaption class="attachment__caption text-center"&gt;
      Droppy
    &lt;/figcaption&gt;
&lt;/figure&gt;

&lt;p&gt;An update to &lt;a href="https://getdroppy.app/"&gt;Droppy&lt;/a&gt; by developer Jordy Spruit dropped this weekend. What started as a free notch app has evolved into a paid, but still inexpensive, suite of Mac productivity tools.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The licensing recently changed so that Droppy’s one-time payment now gets you a license for two Macs instead of one. The change is retroactive and applies to all users. From now until May 31st, the price is €6.99. After that, it will be €9.99. Both prices include lifetime updates, including major version releases.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Droppy is written in native Swift. It’s signed and notarized by Apple, runs on macOS 14 and later, and ships without analytics or third-party trackers.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Spruit says, “v14 contains more than 100 user-visible bug fixes and dozens of performance improvements, all driven by feedback from the Discord testers I’ve been working with daily for months.”&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;My Personal Use Cases&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;In previous versions of Droppy, I’ve used the notch based shelf, the menu bar manager, and the heads up displays extensively while dabbling with the other features. With the extensive additions in the new version, I plan to see what else feels like a good fit for my work style.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Five Functions, One App&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;You can roughly classify what Droppy v14 does into five areas.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ol&gt;
&lt;li&gt;
&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Drag-and-drop shelf that lives in the notch&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;br&gt;Drop files onto it to stash them temporarily, then drag them back out when needed or run quick actions like move, copy, share, zip, unzip, compress, or convert.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;
&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Clipboard Manager&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;br&gt;Includes live previews, pinned and favorited entries, OCR, a built-in screenshot editor, custom tags, and more.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;
&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Floating Shelves&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;br&gt;Droppy calls them “baskets,” but the concept is similar to the shelf in the notch. You can designate watched folders that automatically populate baskets with files, and the interface supports multiple baskets at once.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;
&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Heads-Up Displays (HUDs)&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;br&gt;You can selectively enable notch-based HUDs for things like:&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li class="lexxy-nested-listitem"&gt;&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Volume or brightness changes&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;AirPods connections&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Internet connectivity loss&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;VPN connections&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Low battery warnings&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Music playback&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Notifications&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Caffeine activation to prevent sleep&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;
&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Extensions&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;br&gt;Droppy calls them “Droplets.” These are add-on features that plug into the notch interface.&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ol&gt;

&lt;p&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;There’s no extra charge for extensions&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;, and several of them realistically replace standalone apps.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Included extensions include:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Voice transcription, including live transcription feedback while speaking; something many competing apps still don't offer (new)&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Mechanical keyboard typing sounds routed only through headphones during meetings so you don't blast everyone else on the call&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;An AI coding companion that surfaces activity from Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex directly in the notch, with one-click return to the active app&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;A major overhaul to menu bar management via an internal version of Thaw, a fork of Ice, bundled directly into Droppy&lt;br&gt;Clipboard manager&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Droppy Cloud; a temporary file-sharing service that generates 24-hour share links (new)&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Meeting controls for Zoom, Teams, and similar apps&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Pomodoro timer&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Tiny terminal, and more&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Replacement Suggestions&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Dedicated apps will usually go deeper in specific areas, but if you mainly need solid day-to-day functionality, Droppy v14 could realistically replace:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;MacWhisper or similar transcription apps&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Bartender, Hidden Bar, or Barbee for menu bar management&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Yoink, Gladys, or Unclutter for shelf-style workflows&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Clack or other mechanical keyboard sound apps&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;PastePal, Paste, Copy 'Em, and similar clipboard tools&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Dropover or DropShare&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;A separate Pomodoro timer app&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Some Notable New Features&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;h4&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Droppy Cloud&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/h4&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The sharing limits are generous:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;100 MB per file&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;1 GB per share&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;25 files per share&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;1 GB of active shared data per installation at a time&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The generated links open into an iCloud-style interface with:&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;ul&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Image previews in a grid with click-to-expand&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Inline video and audio playback&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Inline PDF viewing&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;Individual downloads plus “Download All” ZIP support&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;li&gt;A clean, mobile-friendly layout&lt;/li&gt;
&lt;/ul&gt;

&lt;h4&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Lock Screen Display&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/h4&gt;

&lt;p&gt;When playing music in Apple Music, the lock screen now displays expanded album artwork. Synced lyrics scroll over a soft blur effect that keeps them readable even against busy animated art.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h4&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;New UI&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/h4&gt;

&lt;p&gt;According to the developer, every animation in the app has been rebuilt by hand. When the shelf opens, a HUD appears, a widget swaps, or the notch reacts to your cursor, the motion now shares one consistent spring-based feel.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The small floating pill below the notch expands similarly to Dynamic Island on iPhone, and the shelf physically drops down from the notch instead of simply fading in.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Feedback on the Update&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Droppy makes reasonable demands on system resources based on what it does. At idle it consumes about 5% of my M4 CPU and around 275 MB of RAM, about the same amount as the apps, Drafts and Mona for Mastodon use on my system.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;The new interface is subtle, but well executed. Nothing feels over-designed just for the sake of animation demos.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Since Droppy Cloud runs on the developer’s own infrastructure, the 24-hour expiration window makes sense. Features with ongoing hosting costs usually end up behind subscriptions sooner or later, so it’s refreshing to see this included in a one-time purchase.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;I was accustomed to the previous menu bar manager, so the switch to the integrated Thaw-based system took a little adjustment. But after using it for a bit, it feels like a real upgrade rather than a cosmetic replacement. It exposes more functionality than the older implementation and fits better with the rest of the app.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Droppy already does an almost unreasonable number of things, but I still have one request: I’d love to see a lightweight notes or scratchpad interface added somewhere in the ecosystem. Nothing elaborate; just a quick place to park temporary text while working.&lt;/p&gt;

&lt;h2&gt;&lt;b&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Wrap-Up&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/h2&gt;

&lt;p&gt;Droppy v14 feels less like a “notch utility” now and more like a modular productivity platform that happens to live around the notch. Some people will absolutely think it’s trying to do too much. Fair enough. But if your workflow already overlaps with clipboard managers, shelf apps, menu bar utilities, lightweight sharing tools, and small workflow helpers, there’s a good chance Droppy consolidates more of your setup than you’d expect.&lt;/p&gt;

    <summary>An update to Droppy by developer Jordy Spruit dropped this weekend. What started as a free notch app has evolved into a paid, but still inexpensive, suite of Mac productivity tools.

The licensing recently changed so that Droppy’s one-time payment now gets you a license for two Macs instead of one. The...</summary>
